title: Embedder integration playbook — prototypes and quickstart
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a low-friction playbook for engineers who want to embed Redwood Inference into client applications (web/mobile/worker) via our small onboarding SDK layer — called the Embedder kit. The doc covers a compact quickstart, prototype patterns, recommended telemetry and safety checks, common integration mistakes, and a minimal test/gating checklist for rolling from PoC -> pilot. The goal is: get an app calling our hosted embeddings/generation endpoints in under 20 minutes while collecting the minimal signals we need to diagnose performance and quality.

Audience:
- Frontend engineers building product features that rely on embeddings and short-generation calls.
- Backend engineers wiring server-side inference flows and caches.
- SDK integrators and partner engineers building wrappers or plugins.

What this is not:
- Not a comprehensive SDK reference (that's in the API spec).
- Not the final production hardening checklist for Dedicated/Private installs (separate runbook).

Quickstart (5–20 min):
1) Install the embedder kit (npm / pip):
   - npm: npm install @redwood/embedder-kit --save
   - pip: pip install redwood-embedder

2) Minimal config (example, environment-first):
   - REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_demo_key
   - REDWOOD_REGION=us-west1
   - REDWOOD_EMBED_MODEL=redwood-embed-small-v1

3) Example usage (JS):
   const { EmbedClient } = require('@redwood/embedder-kit')
   const client = new EmbedClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
   const vec = await client.embedText('quarterly product brief: summary')

4) Local dev mode: start a dev proxy to replay tokenized responses (dev flag):
   - embedder --dev-proxy --mock-kv

5) Validate: quick smoke test of latency and vector length:
   - call time < 200ms (median on dev account)
   - vector length === 768 for redwood-embed-small-v1

Prototype patterns (pick depending on product constraints):
- Client-side ephemeral calls: great for fast UI demos. Enforce rate-limits, short TTL caches, and never store raw user text in local storage. Use redirect-to-server for sensitive data.
- Server-side batched programmatic embeddings: batch requests (n <= 64) and use our async batch API to reduce per-request cost. Apply prefix caching when input repeats.
- Streaming similarity search: produce embeddings on write, store compressed vectors in our vector-store shim, and run nearest-neighbors on read using approximate search.
- Hybrid approach: light-weight client embedding + server re-ranking for heavy compute.

Recommended config knobs and defaults (opinionated):
- Default model: redwood-embed-small-v1 (balance of cost & quality)
- Batch window: 25ms for UI-first flows, 200ms for background workers
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max retries 3 for 429/5xx
- Cache TTLs: ephemeral UI cache 30s, server-side memo 6h for static content
- Telemetry sampling: 5% for full traces, 100% for error/events

Telemetry & observability (what to collect):
- Minimal events the SDK sends by default (PII-free):
  1) call_started (model, route, region, client_platform)
  2) call_latency_ms (p95, p50, p10)
  3) call_error (http_code, error_class)
  4) vector_size (int)
  5) cache_hit (boolean)
- Enrichers: include app_version, environment (dev/stage/prod), and a sampling token for trace joins.
- Privacy: payloads must never be logged at 100%—only hashed or sampled. Add an opt-in developer flag for capturing request_text in lower environments.

Failure modes & defensive defaults:
- Thundering herd on warmup: enable adaptive backoff and jitter when latency spikes and fail-open to last-known-good cached result when business-critical.
- Partial embeddings (truncated): verify vector length on receipt and mark call_error if mismatch.
- Silent degradations: track rolling baseline of similarity scores on a seed query set; alert if mean similarity drops >10% vs baseline.

Testing matrix (automated checks to include in PR pipeline):
- Unit: embed() returns numeric arrays, deterministic shape unit tests for known inputs.
- Integration: stubbed redwood test server; assert telemetry events emitted, and retry policy triggers on 500s.
- Performance: latency budget test (median & p95 under load) using k6 or similar.
- Quality regression: run prompt set against model and fail build if top-1 similarity for anchor items drops below threshold.

Rollout checklist (PoC -> Pilot -> Production):
- PoC: prototype in dev with 1–2 sample routes, telemetry sampling at 100% for short window, manual quality review.
- Pilot: enable 5–10% real traffic, start cost tracking, gate on latency and quality thresholds.
- Prod: scale sampling down, enable full observability, apply rate limits and quotas, document runbook for incident response.

Canary metrics (gate for expand):
- p95 latency <= target (component-specific)
- error_rate < 0.5%
- similarity_consistency metric deviation < 5%
- cost_per_1000_calls within budget envelope

Common integration pitfalls (and quick mitigations):
- Using largest model by default: pick smaller embedder model for high-volume, then A/B with quality checks.
- Logging raw user text in telemetry: default to hashed text + sample flag.
- Not validating vector shape: add strict shape checks in SDK and return clear errors.
- Blocking UI on server-side reindex: use optimistic UI and background reindex with status indicator.

Developer ergonomics proposals (ideas to iterate on):
- CLI init template that bootstraps minimal config and sample pages for React/Next.js and a Flask worker.
- Playground in console that emulates client calls with telemetry visualizer and model comparator.
- One-click debug trace upload that strips PII and attaches SDK events to a support ticket.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How much payload-level telemetry can we keep by default without increasing compliance burden? (ask security/compliance)
- Should the kit include an optional tiny in-memory vector store for offline dev? tradeoffs: convenience vs divergence from production infra.
- Standardized sampling rates per environment: propose defaults (dev=100%, staging=20%, prod=5%).

Next steps (near term):
- Sync with API team on the batch API surface (owner: Diego).
- Prototype CLI init flow (owner: Elliot) with two example apps (React + Node worker).
- Draft support-runbook template for embedder incidents (owner: Samira).

Appendix: Minimal checklist to ship a PoC
- [ ] Install kit and run quickstart locally
- [ ] Observe telemetry events in dev console
- [ ] Validate vector lengths for sample texts
- [ ] Add unit + integration tests and run through CI
- [ ] Run perf test for median & p95 latency
- [ ] Complete one manual quality check on 10 seed queries

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working draft — focus feedback on missing safety knobs, telemetry fields, and recommended defaults.
- If you want to add an example integration snippet, put it in the /examples folder in the pack repo and link the GH-PR id to linked_artifacts.

---
This doc intentionally favors short, actionable steps and defaults that lower decision friction for front-line engineers. We'll iterate the templates into a more formal quickstart in the product docs once the CLI/init experience is validated.
